text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next, the Bazel config_setting_group //build_config:disable_npu_backend matches @platforms//os:ios, and runtime/executor/BUILD then defines LITERT_DISABLE_NPU for llm_litert_compiled_model_executor_factory, which drops the LlmLiteRtNpuCompiledModelExecutor include and dependency, so iOS builds have no NPU LLM executor.

For the Gemma 4 E4B and E2B .litertlm files, the only dimension MagicNumberConfigsHelper treats as a magic number (a prime greater than 10) is the context size 32003 in the mask inputs: the prefill lengths 1024 and 128 and the decode logits batch 1 are not primes, so AdvancedSettings::prefill_batch_sizes has no effect on these files, and the engine log of a run shows num_configs=1.

sources.detail: Engine log: 'Magic number configs: num_configs=1', 'config[0]: magic_number=32003, target_number=8192'

formula: IsMagicNumber(n) = n >= 11, odd, no odd divisor up to n/2; 32003 is prime; 1024 and 128 are even; 1 < 11

text: In LiteRT-LM's MagicNumberConfigsHelper, the context magic number 32003 is replaced by maxNumTokens when 0 < maxNumTokens < 32003, and otherwise by the largest multiple of 256 below 32003, which is 32,000; so for the E4B and E2B files a maxNumTokens of 32,768 (or anything from 32,003 up) allocates a 32,000-position context, with only a log warning.
conflicts_with: docs/agello/AUDIT.md §2.3 agrees ('32K' runs at 32,000); outline C9: AUDIT's 918 MB vs E4B-GRAPH/T4's 940 MB for the E4B KV cache at 32K

text: In an engine run of agello-next on an Apple M6 with an 8K window and MTP on, LiteRT rewrote the magic number 32003 to 8192 in 577 tensors of the E4B decode signature, 426 of prefill_1024, 581 of verify and 57 of the separate mtp_drafter model, showing that the context config applies to every model compiled in that LiteRT environment.

sources.detail: Engine log lines from magic_number_utils.cc:536 for decode, prefill_1024, verify and mtp_drafter

text: When LlmExecutorSettings::max_num_tokens is 0, EngineSettings::MaybeUpdateAndValidate (called before the LiteRT environment is created) replaces it with LlmMetadata.max_num_tokens if the file sets it, else with ((prompt-hint tokens + 1023) / 4096 + 1) * 4096; the E4B file's LlmMetadata has no max_num_tokens, so an unset maxNumTokens with no prompt hint gives E4B a 4,096-token allocated context.

sources.detail: Metadata: LlmMetadata text has no max_num_tokens field

text: The E4B .litertlm file (Agello's 512-block export) has 24 INT8 KV caches with 2 KV heads, head size 256 for 20 caches and 512 for caches 5, 11, 17 and 23, so the KV cache takes 28,672 bytes per position: 917,504,000 bytes at a 32,000-position allocated context and 939,524,096 bytes at 32,768 positions.

sources.detail: section 10, signature decode: kv_cache_k_N INT8[1,2,32003,256] (512 for 5, 11, 17, 23) and kv_cache_v_N INT8[1,2,256|512,32003]

conflicts_with: outline C9: AUDIT says 918 MB and E4B-GRAPH / T4 say 940 MB for the E4B KV cache at 32K; these are 32,000 and 32,768 positions in decimal MB

text: In LiteRT-LM, FillSingleBufferCacheParamTensor zeroes the INT32 param_tensor input and writes three values: the start position of the update, the end position (start + number of tokens) and the end position again; the Gemma 4 E4B and E2B signatures declare param_tensor as INT32[1,1,1,7], so the remaining four values are 0.

sources.detail: param_tensor INT32[1, 1, 1, 7] in decode, prefill_1024, prefill_128, verify, mtp_drafter

text: LiteRT-LM takes attention mask types and the sliding window only from a file's ExecutorMetadata (GetAttentionMaskParams defaults to causal global and local masks with no window); the Gemma 4 E4B and E2B .litertlm files have no ExecutorMetadata section, so the compiled-model executor fills causal mask rows for image placeholder tokens too, and FillAttentionMask's vision-bidirectional branch never runs for them.

In an agello-next engine run of E4B on an Apple M6 (2,049 prompt tokens, MTP on), the mask_fills counter was 4, equal to runs_prefill (3) plus runs_decode (1), so ShouldSkipGlobalCausalAttentionMask did not skip E4B's CPU-filled mask on Metal: the executor filled it for every prefill run and plain decode step.

On the GPU, LiteRT-LM's GetOptimizedPrefillWorkGroups splits a prompt across E4B's prefill_1024 and prefill_128 signatures as: 130 tokens -> 128 + 2 (two prefill_128 runs); 700 -> one prefill_1024 run holding 700; 1,500 -> 1024 + 128 + 128 + 128 + 92; 1,600 -> 1024 + 576 (two prefill_1024 runs); 2,049 -> 1024 + 1024 + 1 (the last in prefill_128); on the CPU the remainder always cascades to prefill_128 (700 -> 5 x 128 + 60).
formula: Cautious greedy: full chunks of 1024; remainder r goes to one more padded 1024 run if 2r >= 1024, else to 128-token runs (128 x floor(r/128) plus the rest in a last prefill_128 run); recomputed with a Python port of the function

text: In an agello-next engine run of E4B on an Apple M6, a 2,049-token prompt took 3 prefill runs (runs_prefill = 3), matching GetOptimizedPrefillWorkGroups' split into prefill_1024, prefill_1024 and a 1-token prefill_128 run.
formula: 2049 = 2 x 1024 + 1; remainder 1 < 512 so it goes to prefill_128: 3 runs

text: LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Prefill decides once whether any prefill input buffer is Metal memory (TensorBuffer::IsMetalMemory) and, if so, runs every prefill work group synchronously with CompiledModel::Run (TODO b/494284915), so on Metal prefill runs never overlap with the CPU's preparation of the next chunk.

Our agello-next commit e43f9a8d changed LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase so a plain decode step no longer copies the whole processed-token history to fill the attention mask (it passes an empty token-id span, since a decode query is never an image placeholder) and reuses one sampled-ids TensorBuffer (DecodeOutputTokens) while its [batch, length] shape is unchanged, instead of allocating one per step.
conflicts_with: docs/agello/AUDIT.md §2.3 (v0.18.0 line numbers) describes a mask refill 'with a copy of the whole token history' and 'a new host ids buffer per step' per decode step: true of v0.18.0, not of agello-next

text: For Gemma 4 E4B on the GPU in agello-next, each plain decode step does this on the CPU: runs the text embedder model (2,560 floats out) and the per-layer embedder model (42 x 256 floats out) for the token, copies both (53,248 bytes) into the decode input buffers, writes input_pos and param_tensor, resets and fills the attention mask (one byte per allocated position), and, with the GPU sampler unavailable, samples on the CPU from the 262,144-entry logits.

sources.detail: decode inputs embeddings [1,1,2560], per_layer_embeddings [1,1,42,256], mask BOOL[1,1,1,32003]; logits [1,1,262144]

text: LiteRT-LM's EmbeddingLookupText compiles the token and per-layer embedder models with HwAccelerators::kCpu on every platform except Android (where NPU is added), and each lookup runs that CompiledModel on one token id, so on iOS and macOS every embedding lookup is a CPU model run.

In an agello-next engine run of E4B on an Apple M6 (2,049 prompt tokens, 17 generated, MTP on), the embedding_lookups counter was 4,098: two lookups (embedder and per-layer) for each of the 1,023 tokens prefilled in each of the two prefill_1024 slices, plus two for the pending token of each of the three MTP rounds after the first.

LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Create picks the LitertState allocation policy kInplace on the CPU, kGpuOptimizedInplace on the GPU when the decode signature has a param_tensor input (all Gemma 4 .litertlm files), and kPingPong (two banks swapped on every GetStateBuffers call) on the GPU otherwise; under kGpuOptimizedInplace the KV buffers are created as GPU output buffers and, for files without ExecutorMetadata, never bound as inputs.

Our agello-next commits aec81cb7 and 585203d3 make LitertState::DeepCopy snapshot KV caches by copying each shared MTLBuffer's bytes as they are (GPU layout, no lock conversion) into page-aligned mmap'd host memory, when every state buffer is a Metal buffer with a shared MTLBuffer of its own (length within 64 KiB of the tensor's packed size); CopyContentsFrom restores such a snapshot byte for byte, and the Metal helper is built only for ios and macos (a stub elsewhere).

In our agello-next build, CreateSampler for a GPU sampler backend finds no Metal TopK sampler (the closed library isn't linked), falls back to the CPU TopPSampler and records a sampler_fallback_to_cpu anomaly; an engine run on an Apple M6 recorded sampler = cpu (GPU sampler unavailable), while Google's prebuilt v0.18.0 binary defines 39 TopK Metal sampler symbols to our 7.

sources.detail: Facts: sampler = cpu (GPU sampler unavailable); Anomalies: sampler_fallback_to_cpu x1

text: LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Create allocates the decode logits buffer as FP16 when the backend is GPU, activations are FP16 and GetSamplerBackend resolves to GPU (an unspecified sampler backend means the main backend), regardless of whether a GPU sampler can later be created; with default settings on the GPU the CPU fallback sampler therefore receives FP16 logits.
conflicts_with: docs/agello/AUDIT.md §2.4: 'FP16 logits only with FP16 precision and the GPU sampler' (true if 'GPU sampler' means the sampler backend setting, not a loaded GPU sampler); related to outline C13

text: LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::InitializeSampler lets a GPU sampler drive decode inputs (sampler_handles_input) only if the setting allows it, the sampler can handle input, embeddings are computed in the graph (no CPU embedding lookup), the model has a token-id input and no local mask; Gemma 4 E4B and E2B take embeddings instead of token ids, so this path is never used for them on any backend.

sources.detail: decode inputs: embeddings, per_layer_embeddings, no token_ids/tokens input

text: LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter sets the number of draft steps to the verify signature's input_pos length minus one; the Gemma 4 E4B and E2B files have verify input_pos INT32[4], so MTP drafts 3 tokens per round and a round emits 1 to 4 tokens.

In LiteRT-LM's MTP, the verify run takes the token being extended plus the 3 drafts at positions p..p+3, and the number of accepted drafts is the longest prefix on which the drafts equal the verifier's greedy picks (CountAcceptedPrefix); the round emits the accepted drafts plus the verifier's next pick as a bonus token, and current_step advances by that count.

LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter creates both its drafter and verifier samplers as greedy (TOP_P with k = 1), so with speculative decoding on, every token after a decode call's priming step is the argmax of the main model's verify logits, whatever the session's temperature, top-k or top-p; only the priming plain decode step uses the session's sampler.

In an agello-next engine run of E4B on an Apple M6 (17 generated tokens, MTP on), MTP ran 4 rounds that drafted 12 tokens and accepted all 12, with 12 drafter runs, 4 verify runs and 1 plain decode run (the priming step), giving 1 + 4 x 4 = 17 tokens.

sources.detail: Counters: mtp_rounds 4, mtp_drafted 12, mtp_accepted 12, runs_drafter 12, runs_verify 4, runs_decode 1, tokens_decoded 17

formula: 1 priming token + 4 rounds x (3 accepted + 1 bonus) = 17; drafter runs = 4 x 3 = 12

text: In LiteRT-LM v0.18.0 (what Agello ships), the compiled-model executor skips the MTP priming step whenever the last run was a decode (RuntimeState::ran_decode), with no separate flag invalidated by plain decode steps, restores or step changes; agello-next's upstream code adds mtp_primed_ for that, while the acceptance rule (longest matching prefix) is the same in both.

For Gemma 4 E4B, the vision executor's patch_num_shrink_factor is 9: the vision encoder's first signature (vision_140) takes 1,260 patches and the first adapter signature outputs 140 tokens; GetVitSignatureIndex then picks the smallest vision_70/140/280 signature whose token count is at least the image's patches divided by 9.

sources.detail: section 7 vision_140 images [1,1260,768]; section 8 vision_adapter_140 mm_embedding [1,140,2560]

text: LiteRT-LM's EngineSettings::CreateDefault hard-codes the vision and audio adapter backends to CPU (comment: 'Vision adapter can only run on CPU'), and the Gemma 4 E4B and E2B files also mark tf_lite_vision_adapter backend_constraint=cpu; the engine validates only the constraints of the main (tf_lite_prefill_decode), vision-encoder and audio-encoder sections, not the adapters'.

Agello's ChatEngine.makeEngine passes .cpu() as both the vision backend and the audio backend of LiteRT-LM's EngineConfig, so in the app the vision encoder (not only the adapter) and the audio encoder run on the CPU.

For Gemma 4 E4B, the audio executor treats the encoder as static (inputs mask and src_inputs, no prev_ state inputs, and an adapter is present) with a shrink factor of 4: the encoder mask has 816 elements and the adapter outputs 204 rows, so each 816-frame window yields up to 204 audio tokens.

sources.detail: section 4 serving_default mask BOOL[1,1,816], src_inputs [1,1,816,128]; section 5 audio_adapter output_0 [1,204,2560]

text: The Gemma 4 E4B and E2B files mark tf_lite_audio_encoder_hw backend_constraint=cpu, and EngineSettings::MaybeUpdateAndValidate checks it with ValidateBackendConstraint, so creating an engine with a non-CPU audio backend for these files fails with 'Audio backend constraint mismatch'.

The embeddinggemma-2-text-270m .litertlm file's text encoder has signatures encoder_1x128, 1x256, 1x512, 1x1024, 1x2048 and 1x8192 taking embeddings [1, n, 512] and a FLOAT32 input_mask and returning encodings [1, 768]; EmbeddingLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor uses the smallest signature at least as long as the input.

sources.detail: signatures encoder_1x128 ... encoder_1x8192: embeddings [1,n,512], input_mask [1,n], encodings [1,768]

text: EmbeddingLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor handles inputs longer than its largest encoder signature with ComputeEmbeddingOptions::input_overflow_strategy, which defaults to kError (an InvalidArgument error); kTruncate cuts to the largest signature (optionally keeping EOS ids at the end) and kChunkAndAverage averages the embeddings of consecutive chunks.

Our agello-next commit 645aaf65 makes CreateCompilationOptions set the GPU sync wait type to kPassive outside benchmark mode (kActive in benchmark mode); LiteRT-LM v0.18.0 sets kActive in benchmark mode and leaves the delegate's default otherwise.

LiteRT-LM v0.18.0 (the source of what Agello ships) resets and refills the decode attention mask every step from a full copy of the processed-token history, allocates a new sampled-ids buffer every decode step, and snapshots KV state with CopyTensorBuffer through a tensor-buffer lock; agello-next drops the history copy and reuses the ids buffer (ours: e43f9a8d) and copies raw MTLBuffer bytes on Apple (ours: aec81cb7, 585203d3).

When the decode logits batch exceeds 1, LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic keeps a decode-only LitertState of that batch, broadcasts the prefill state into it on the first decode step and copies candidate 0 back before the next prefill; MTP requires a batch of 1.
LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Create skips LoRA inputs of the decode signature (IsLoRAInputName) when creating decode input buffers, leaving them to the LoRA manager.

Agello's ChatEngine.load sets LiteRT-LM's ExperimentalFlags.enableBenchmark = true; the Swift Engine then calls litert_lm_engine_settings_enable_benchmark, which creates the engine's benchmark parameters, so EngineSettings::IsBenchmarkEnabled is true and MaybeUpdateAndValidate sets AdvancedSettings::is_benchmark; CreateCompilationOptions then requests the active GPU wait (SyncExecutionModeWaitType::kActive), in agello-next (bypassing our passive-wait commit 645aaf65) and in v0.18.0 alike.

At agello-next 7b872544, LlmExecutorBaseInterface, LlmExecutorExternalSamplerInterface and LlmExecutorInternalSamplerInterface (runtime/executor/llm_executor_interface.h) have no implementation or user outside their header and Bazel target; the executors implement LlmExecutorBase (alias LlmExecutor).

LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase (subclasses Static and Dynamic) implements LlmExecutor and is not instantiable itself; its class comment calls it a GPU executor although the static subclass also serves the CPU backend.
Tasks calls the executor synchronously on the execution thread: Decode(decode_params) for internal sampling and DecodeLogits(inputs) for external sampling.

CreateLlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor sends CPU and GPU backends to the static or dynamic compiled-model executor based on IsDynamicModel (ExecutorMetadata state buffers if present, else dynamic dimensions of the first prefill signature's KV inputs and positions), and NPU to LlmLiteRtNpuCompiledModelExecutor when the file has a TF_LITE_AUX section, falling back to the CPU/GPU path with the generic compiler plugin otherwise.
The Gemma 4 E4B and E2B files have fixed-size KV inputs and no ExecutorMetadata section, so IsDynamicModel returns false and they run on LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic.

sources.detail: Sections: no ExecutorMetadata; kv_cache inputs have no -1 dimension

text: LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Create creates the embedding lookups and (if the engine's enable_speculative_decoding is set) the MTP drafter, picks the first prefill* signature (filtered by selected_signatures, which must include decode), creates the LitertState, clamps maxNumTokens to its entries, creates non-KV decode buffers, a decode-only state when the logits batch exceeds 1, and the prefill runner set keyed by sequence length, largest first.

In EngineAdvancedImpl's streaming load path, the engine compiles the main model and, when enable_speculative_decoding is set, the drafter itself and passes both to CreateLlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor; it skips the drafter's weights when the engine-level flag is off.

LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorDynamic requires the CPU backend, compiles with FP32 activations, uses the in-place KV policy, splits prefill into CpuConfig::prefill_chunk_size chunks (none at -1), and grows the KV cache by CpuConfig::kv_increment_size entries when decode reaches its end, copying the old contents into new buffers.

GetModelSignaturesFromInputOutputNames maps input names token_ids/tokens, positions/input_pos, attn_mask/mask, local_mask/attn_mask_local/local_attn_mask, embeddings, per_layer_embeddings and param_tensor, and the output name logits, to their roles; in strict mode it requires tokens or embeddings, positions and logits.

The engine log in generated/engine-run.md lists decode, prefill_1024 and verify (subgraphs 0, 1, 3) but not prefill_128 (subgraph 2) because gen_empirical.py keeps the first occurrence of each message with digits replaced, folding prefill_128's line into prefill_1024's; the file itself has prefill_128.

sources.detail: Engine log: 'Loaded: num_subgraphs=1340, num_signatures=4' and three signature lines

text: CreateEnvironment builds magic-number LiteRT environment options with MagicNumberConfigsHelper for CPU, GPU and generic-plugin NPU backends unless AdvancedSettings::configure_magic_numbers is false, and passes them as kMagicNumberConfigs (plus kMagicNumberVerifications when verify_magic_numbers is set).
MagicNumberConfigsHelper maps prefill-length magic numbers, in ascending order, to AdvancedSettings::prefill_batch_sizes or to defaults, and caps each prefill target at the context target.

For files without ExecutorMetadata, LitertState's heuristic creation takes the context size from the last dimension of the prefill signature's mask input (or the key cache's third dimension if there is no mask), and the static executor then lowers maxNumTokens to that size (ClampMaxNumTokens).

In PrefillInternal the executor writes consecutive input_pos values from current_step, looks up embeddings and per-layer embeddings for the slice's tokens with the CPU EmbeddingLookupManager (or copies embeddings passed in the inputs when there is no lookup), fills the attention mask unless skipped, and fills param_tensor when the model has one.
FillInputBufferWithToken writes each token's id (if it has no embedding) or its embedding or per-layer embedding vector into one row of the input buffer and zero-fills the rest of the row.
The executor fills param_tensor with update length = the run's token count for prefill (the whole slice), 1 for decode, num_draft_steps + 1 for verify and 1 for each drafter run.

With GPU external-tensor mode off (the default), CreateCompilationOptions adds param_tensor (and kv_cache_, w_prime, lora_, and logits for a GPU sampler) to the external-tensor patterns and marks param_tensor, kv_cache_ (with a param_tensor), w_prime and lora_ for buffer storage; it also sets the hint that prefill and decode are fully delegated to one delegate.

InitializeAttentionMask fills the mask with masked values (false for BOOL, -45824 for FP16, -45824 or -0.7 x FLT_MAX for FP32 depending on precision) before FillAttentionMask opens the causal (and windowed, if configured) range for each query row.

ShouldSkipGlobalCausalAttentionMask skips the CPU mask only on the GPU backend with a param_tensor, a causal global mask (and causal local mask if present), and a BOOL mask buffer that fell back to host memory because the GPU graph doesn't read it.

PrefillInternal processes the pending token from the previous call first, then all but the last token of the slice; the last token becomes the new pending token with its embeddings looked up immediately, so a slice of n tokens fills n positions when a token was pending and n - 1 otherwise, and a 1-token slice with no pending token runs nothing.
Unused rows of a prefill input get the pad token id (0 when the settings have none) on the token-id path, and the embedding of token 0 on the embedding path.

LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorStatic::Prefill passes the remaining capacity (state entries minus current_step) to GetOptimizedPrefillWorkGroups, which drops larger signatures and fails with FailedPrecondition when the tokens don't fit; on the CPU backend it uses greedy chunking.

A plain Decode step runs DecodeLogitsImpl (PrepareFirstDecode, GetTokenToDecode, DecodeInternal, constraint masking), then SampleLogits into the ids buffer, reads the ids back, replaces negative ids by 0 (or errors with error_on_invalid_sampled_token_id) and keeps the last id as the pending token.
BindTensorsAndRunDecode calls CompiledModel::RunAsync for decode; in an agello-next engine run on an Apple M6 the telemetry recorded gpu_async = unavailable: no post-dispatch event.

sources.detail: Facts: gpu_async = unavailable: no post-dispatch event

text: Each MTP draft step looks up one token embedding on the CPU, copies it with the previous activations into the drafter's activations input, runs the drafter and samples greedily; each verification looks up embeddings and per-layer embeddings for all 4 tokens, fills a 4-row mask and samples greedily over 4 logit rows.
LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::Reset and SetCurrentStep only move current_step (and clear the MTP-primed flag); the KV contents are kept and overwritten as positions are reused.
AdvancedSettings::clear_kv_cache_before_prefill (default true) zeroes the first bank of KV buffers once, when LitertState allocates them, not before every prefill.

The KV-token deletion helpers in llm_litert_compiled_model_cache_utils.h (ShouldDeleteKVCacheTokens, DeleteTokensFromKvCache, DeleteTokensIfNeeded) have no non-test callers at agello-next 7b872544, so the compiled-model executor never evicts tokens from a full KV cache.

RestoreState copies a host-memory snapshot into the live GPU KV buffers (CopyContentsFrom) instead of swapping it in, because GPU delegates keep using the buffers they bound; upstream CopyTensorBuffer snapshots Metal buffers into host buffers through a lock as a workaround for a Metal buffer leak.
LitertState::SelectAndCopyFrom and BroadcastAndCopyFrom copy one candidate's caches in and out of the multi-candidate decode state with memcpy through locks and refuse ping-pong states.

With internal sampling (the default), the executor creates its sampler lazily from the session RuntimeConfig's sampler parameters, defaulting to greedy TOP_P with k = 1, on the backend GetSamplerBackend returns (the main backend when unspecified, CPU for NPU).

External sampling happens only when SessionConfig::UseExternalSampler() is true (false by default); the threaded execution manager then creates a CPU sampler for the session, rejects other sampler backends, and Tasks samples logits returned by DecodeLogits.

Without the engine-level enable_speculative_decoding, a session that asks for speculative decoding makes EnsureMtpDrafterLoaded create the drafter on its first decode, which requires the model resources, a single output head and the embedding lookup.
For each Decode call the compiled-model executor uses MTP when the decode params' enable_speculative_decoding is true, or, when it is unset, whenever a drafter is loaded.
The MTP drafter has no KV cache of its own: LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter binds its kv_cache_* inputs to the main model's state buffers; for E4B it reads caches 22 and 23, for E2B caches 13 and 14.

LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft sets the drafter's input_pos, mask and param_tensor once per round, for the position before the token being extended, and every draft step of the round uses them; only the activations input changes between steps.

Each draft step's activations input is the last token's embedding concatenated with the previous activations: the decode or verifier activations at the first step, then the drafter's projected_activations (5,120 = 2 x 2,560 values for E4B).

When mtp_primed_ is false (after a prefill, a plain decode step, a context or state restore, a step change or a failed round), an MTP Decode call first runs one plain decode step with the session's sampler and passes its token and decode activations to the drafter.

MtpRoundStats records drafted, accepted and emitted tokens and drafting and verification times for the last round; the executor accumulates them per round in ExecutorStats and counts the priming step as a plain step.

LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Create compiles the tf_lite_mtp_drafter section with the main executor's compilation options under its own cache suffix and, on the GPU, adds kv_cache_ and param_tensor as external, buffer-storage tensors.

VisionLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor::Encode (map form) runs the chosen vision encoder signature, counts valid tokens from its mask output, writes the valid feature rows into the matching adapter signature, runs the adapter and returns its output rows in a new host buffer.

The static executor's Prefill registers vision and audio embeddings with the EmbeddingLookupManager, which writes their rows in place of the placeholder ids -1 (image) and -2 (audio) during prefill lookups; end-of-image and end-of-audio rows come from the tf_lite_end_of_vision and tf_lite_end_of_audio models.
VisionAdapter::Initialize's GPU branch sets GPU cache options but never calls SetHardwareAccelerators, unlike the encoder's GPU branch.

AudioLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor::Create chooses a streaming encoder when the encoder has prev_ inputs or there is no adapter and a static encoder otherwise; a static encoder processes audio in windows of its sequence length without overlap.

EmbeddingLiteRtCompiledModelExecutor looks up token (and per-layer) embeddings with the same EmbeddingLookupManager as the LLM, writes an input_mask of 1.0 for real tokens and 0.0 for padding, and runs the text encoder on the configured backend (CPU via XNNPACK, GPU, or NPU where compiled in).
Agello's embedder loads EmbeddingGemma with the GPU backend first and falls back to the CPU backend if that fails.

Under #if defined(__APPLE__), CreateCompilationOptions turns texture weights off and passes gpu_enable_metal_residency_set (default false) to the GPU options, and GetRunOptions repeats the residency-set choice on every run.

In an agello-next engine run of E4B on an Apple M6, tensor-buffer locks copied 15,419,392 bytes (host_lock_copy_bytes) and unlocks 259,257,252 bytes (host_unlock_copy_bytes) through 30 host shadow allocations.
On macOS the agello-next engine log shows 'NPU accelerator could not be loaded and registered: kLiteRtStatusErrorNotFound', so the NPU path is unavailable there too.
litert_lm_engine_settings_set_prefill_chunk_size only changes CpuConfig::prefill_chunk_size; with a non-CPU backend it logs a warning and returns OK without effect.
LlmExecutorSettings::CreateDefault gives the CPU backend kv_increment_size 16, prefill_chunk_size -1 and 4 threads, the GPU backend max_top_k 64, and sets max_num_tokens to 0.
EmbeddingLookupManager::LookupDecode rejects negative (multimodal placeholder) token ids with 'Multimodal embeddings are not supported during decode'.
